31 August 2026 Our Ref: INS/TEC/3/35 
 
 By Email Only 
 
 
  
To: Chief Executives of all authorized insurers  
 
 
 
Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Integrity Management Policy 
 
To ensure healthy development of  the insurance industry, it is 
imperative for authorized insurers to ma intain a high standard of corporate 
governance and a sound internal control sy stem.  One of the vital elements of 
corporate governance and internal controls  is integrity management.  Integrity 
should be prioritized at the Board level by fostering a corporate culture across the 
insurer that ensures all business practices carried out by it, or on its behalf, are 
conducted honestly and with integrity.  This should include establishing an 
integrity management policy that must be complied with by all directors, 
controllers as defined in section 13A(12) of the Insurance Ordinance (Cap. 41), 
key persons in control functions, staff and agents1 of the insurer.  As such, clear 
and well-communicated integrity standards should be in place, where integrity is 
embedded in the insurer’s internal cont rol system, through robust mechanisms 
for the reporting and enforcement of non-compliance, as well as through regular 
reviews of integrity management policies and procedures.   
 
In this regard, all authorized insu rers are required to formulate an 
integrity management policy or enhance their existing policy with reference to 
the sample of integrity mana gement policy set out in the Annex by 1 January 
2027.  The sample of integrity manageme nt policy outlines expectations on the 
essential governance aspects relating to pr obity including, but not limited to, (i) 
anti-bribery requirements (prohibiting the offer, solicitation or acceptance of 
advantages), (ii) avoidance and management  of conflicts of interest (requiring 
avoidance of conflicts, declaration and proper management of  conflicts), (iii) 
preservation of confidentiality, and (i v) enforcement and reporting of non-
 
1 According to the Prevention of Bribery Ordinance (Cap. 201), “agent” includes any person employed by or 
acting for another.  In the context of an authorized insurer, an “agent” includes insurance agents, consultants, or 
any persons employed by or acting for the insurer. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
2  
compliance – including corruption – and the provision of assistance to regulatory 
authorities and law enforcement agencies.  
 
For HK insurers and designated insu rers, the integrity management 
policy should apply at the entity level, whereas for non- HK insurers (other than 
designated insurers), the integrity ma nagement policy should apply to the 
insurance business carried on by them in or from Hong Kong.  
 
Should you have any questions in re lation to the above, please contact 
your case officer or email us at enquiry@ia.org.hk. 
 
 
Yours faithfully, 
 
 
 
 
 
Clement Lau  
Executive Director  
Policy and Legislation 
Insurance Authority 
 
  
Encl. 
 
c.c. Chairman, The Hong K ong Federation of Insurers
